transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Thanks for coming back in, Mr. Lindqvist. I wanted to follow up on those questions you had after our last talk.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Right. Because the last talk left me with a lot of questions, to be honest. I've been thinking about it all week.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this has been a stressful situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stressful isn't the word. I'm a former paramedic. I know how a referral chain works. You don't just mark a developmental screening as completed because a parent missed one appointment. That's not how the SOP works.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: So, looking into the chart, the referral was entered, but after that first appointment was declined, the status was changed to completed in the EHR without any further follow-up attempts being logged.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Exactly. It was falsified. In any other context, we'd call that a falsified record. Who did it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a failure in the administrative process, the system essentially allowed the task to be closed out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop blaming the software. A human being clicked the button. A human being decided that a child's developmental screen was finished when it never happened. Do you get that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you're feeling very angry about how this was handled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm beyond angry. I'm disgusted. My kid missed a critical window for screening because someone wanted to clear their task list. Was this a systemic failure or just laziness?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just that we've been incredibly short-staffed lately and things can get overlooked when the volume is this high.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care if you're running a war zone. You don't fake a completed screening. I want a written apology and I want to know exactly what is being done to make sure this doesn't happen to someone else.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to move through a few more things on the clinical side today, but we can look at the next steps now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't give a damn about your schedule. I'm talking about my son's healthcare.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is frustrating, but let's just focus on the plan to get him seen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're dodging the accountability. Did you apologize for the error?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry for any confusion the scheduling process caused.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? This wasn't a misunderstanding of a date. This was a failure of care. You're speaking in circles.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, the fact is the screening didn't happen. But we can fix it now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine. How?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have already contacted the developmental pediatrician's office. I've requested an expedited slot. I'll call you by tomorrow at 4 PM to give you the exact date and time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what do I do in the meantime?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just keep a log of any specific behaviors you've noticed at home so you can hand it to the specialist. That'll help the assessment move faster.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I've already got a log. I'm a clinician, remember? I've been tracking this for months.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, well, that will be useful.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This doesn't change the fact that the record was wrong. Are you going to correct the chart or just leave the lie there?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll make sure a note is added to the file explaining the delay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A note. Great. So the history will just say it was delayed, not that it was prematurely closed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I think that's the best way to handle it for now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's not. It's a cover-up.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really do understand that this is upsetting for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You don't understand. You're just trying to get me out of the office.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want to make sure we have a clear path forward for your son.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The path forward is for someone to actually take responsibility. Not the system. Not the staffing. A person.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: As I said, it was a failure in the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're still doing it. You're still using the passive voice.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm trying to explain the facts as they are.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The fact is you're not apologizing for the mistake, you're apologizing for my reaction to it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've told you we're getting him in quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which you should have done months ago.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll call you tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'll be waiting for that call. And if I don't hear from you by four, I'm calling the Patient Advocate's office.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That's fine. I'll have the appointment time for you.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language ('I have to move through a few more things', 'let's just focus on the plan') and shows defensive escalation under pushback.

E.justification: The error is named (referral status changed to completed without follow-up), but there are no comprehension checks throughout the interaction.

A.justification: Responsibility is consistently deflected to 'the administrative process', 'the system', and 'short-staffed' conditions.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('angry', 'upsetting') and acknowledges the patient's frustration.

T.justification: Resident provides a specific next step (expedited slot), a clear timeline (call by tomorrow at 4 PM), a patient role (keep a log of behaviors), and addresses prevention (adding a note to the file).
